occurrences.rawText: Introduction Trust Funds1 are financial and administrative arrangements made between Development Partners (DPs) and one or more World Bank Group entities to meet diverse development needs including project preparation, technical assistance, advisory services, debt relief, post conflict transition, disaster recovery, climate change, and co-financing of lending projects. Trust funds contribute to the Bank Group’s mission of poverty reduction on a livable planet by supporting the design and implementation of development projects.

occurrences.rawText: This report provides aggregate financial information on trust fund operations administered individually or jointly by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), the International Development Association (IDA), the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA). These four entities are collectively referred to as the “Bank Group.” This report is unaudited, and is not intended to represent the combined financial position of trust funds and programs administered by the Bank Group. Numbers presented for previous periods have been regrouped to conform to the current period presentation.

occurrences.nextContext: Ukraine continues to receive support from the international community. In YTD FY26, contribution receivables from Japan, through the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), have reached $2,470m. This contribution is being provided i

occurrences.rawText: Ukraine continues to receive support from the international community. In YTD FY26, contribution receivables from Japan, through the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), have reached $2,470m. This contribution is being provided in installments over several years. Further, Ukraine disbursements with IBRD as Implementing Entity reached $7,372m ($1,000m in YTD FY25), equivalent to a 637% increase compared to the previous year. Disbursement amounts vary depending on the timing and verification of eligible expenditures submitted by the Ukrainian government.

occurrences.rawText: TF reforms continued in YTD FY26 with an aim to reduce fragmentation, increase strategic alignment and improve efficiencies of the trust fund portfolio by using fewer and larger Umbrella 2.0 Programs. As of December 31, 2025, 75 Umbrella programs (146 active trust funds) have been established. CWA and DPI TF are new programs established in YTD FY26. occurrences.rawText: Commitment authority represents an upper limit up to which task teams can commit future disbursements at the individual TF level. The classes of assets that a trust fund could commit upon form the trust fund’s Basis of Commitment (BoC). The asset classes that can be committed against are either (i) cash, (ii) cash plus promissory notes, or (iii) cash plus promissory notes and contributions receivable. The default BoC for a trust fund is cash, but may be modified to include promissory notes receivable and/or contributions receivable with the approval of Director(s) in the unit managing the trust fund. occurrences.nextContext: Cash received from DPs contributions, loans from DPs and proceeds from the issuance of bonds (for IFFIM) are managed by IBRD’s Treasury, which manages a commingled investment portfolio (the Pool) for all funds that are administered by the B

occurrences.rawText: Cash received from DPs contributions, loans from DPs and proceeds from the issuance of bonds (for IFFIM) are managed by IBRD’s Treasury, which manages a commingled investment portfolio (the Pool) for all funds that are administered by the Bank Group entities. The Pool also includes funds held in ICSID's escrow accounts. IBRD maintains all assets underlying the trust funds’ fund balances separate and apart from the assets of the World Bank Group. IBRD, on behalf of the World Bank Group, invests the funds in liquid financial instruments such as government and agency obligations, time deposits, money-market securities and asset-backed securities, as well as swaps and a range of other derivative instruments. Additionally, the pool also include equity securities. The investment composition within the pool is based on the investment horizons and cash flow profiles of the trust fund programs. Net investment income earned by the Pool is allocated to each trust fund based on its share of cash and investments in the Pool.
